title: Franklin Street musicians and Tick Chambers; band photo question
summary: Keppard names players on Franklin Street around Tick Chambers and the district closing; the tape ends with a question about a band photo with Roy Palmer.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Oakland right where Crozac is. Dates have their back entrance that Hall is given back there. Old man Umpra used to play with dear with Tick Chambers. You heard to talk about Tick Chambers? Yes, the Oakland Well, Tickshaber was playing cornet, and this fellow, Lawrence Dewitt, was playing clarinet at that time with him. And the old man, Umpra, was playing cyborg, clarinet over there with him also. Well, after he left, well, and the district closed down, well, they all reopened up with this fellow, little Willie Jackson. He was around there on Franklin between Beemble and Ourville. But this fellow, Tickshaber, was on Franklin between Coddall and Ourville, right back across from Basin Street. But when they closed the district down, at the time they had that humbug in, I just remember what year it was, when Jim the Blood came down here and he shot Billy Phillips. Where did the tuxedo? That was the tuxedo. That was the tuxedo, and this is at the back there. Now Billy Phillips, now, this here fellow, what they called, they had two brothers of them, had the saloon. Right there, what they call again, uh... Entertainer? 25, Franklin Street. That was, uh, let me see, I'm trying to get it together. It was 25, 28 Franklin was...

You know, the rest of it. You know, it's just like, yeah, you see that voice note? Just like I said, well, I'm going to play in E-flat. All right, that voice note. Well, all the rest of the modern keys will follow right behind the system, brother. See? And every time they change, you can hear change, and in you lose. Is that going on here? Yes. Yes. I want to ask about this band, the one picture you have with Roy Palmer and Lawrence Dewey and Sugar Johnny. Yes, well, I'll tell you.
